artists.biography: The Smiths were an English alternative rock band, formed in Manchester in 1982. Based on the song writing partnership of Morrissey (vocals) and Johnny Marr (guitar), the band also included Andy Rourke (bass) and Mike Joyce (drums). Critics have called them the most important alternative rock band to emerge from the British independent music scene of the 1980s. The group was signed to the independent record label Rough Trade Records, on which they released four studio albums, several compilations, and numerous non-LP singles. Although they had limited commercial success outside the UK while they were still together, and never released a single that charted higher than number 10 in their home country, The Smiths won a significant following, and remain cult and commercial favourites. The band broke up in 1987 and have turned down several offers to reunite since then.

perplexity.description:
Best... I is a 1992 compilation by The Smiths, released by WEA after the band’s back catalogue changed hands. It collects 14 of the group’s best-known tracks from their 1983–1987 run, and it became a major commercial success, reaching No. 1 on the UK Albums Chart and No. 139 in the United States.

Musically, the set is a concise overview of The Smiths’ signature sound: jangling guitars, melodic bass lines, and Morrissey’s sharply literate, emotionally fraught lyrics. The tracklist includes defining songs such as “This Charming Man,” “How Soon Is Now?,” “Stop Me If You Think You’ve Heard This One Before,” and “Please, Please, Please, Let Me Get What I Want,” making it one of the most accessible entry points into the band’s catalog.

Because it is a hits collection rather than a studio album, Best... I works less as a unified artistic statement than as a summary of The Smiths’ impact on British indie rock. Its chart performance and continued reissues reflect the enduring demand for the band’s most celebrated singles and album tracks.
